text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--- Neighbours to a former factory in Copenhagen recently bought by the Hells Angels bike gang are asking prime minister Poul Nyrup Rasmussen to help them get rid of the bikers as they fear getting caught in the crossfire of the gang war between the Angels and the rival Bandidos.

--- All political parties in the parliament are demanding that an independent survey on conditions for the uneducated and chronically unemployed is published and not kept from the public by the ministry of finance.

--- The number of Danes who die alone in their homes and are only found weeks after is increasing. In ten years the number of dead people found alone in their homes increased by 40 percent to 7,091 last year. Doctors and ambulance staff see the increase as a sign of extensive loneliness among elderly people.

--- Pressure is expected to be put on John Iversen, the sole member of the European parliament representing SF - the leftist Socialist People's Party - to resign his seat in Strasbourg after he formally quits the party today. Iversen is switching allegiance to the ruling Social Democratic Party.

Iversen, a pro-European in a party basically opposed to closer European Union, has been with SF for 22 years and a member of the European parliament from 1985 until 1994. He resumed his seat in Strasbourg a year ago after a spell as spokesman for Danish environmental commissioner Ritt Bjerregaard in Brussels.
--- More than 2000 postal service employees are to lose their jobs within the next two to three years due to new automation of postal sorting.

--- Tax minister Carsten Koch thinks that the Internet could undermine Danish tax and VAT as Danes can now buy goods abroad via the Internet without paying any VAT. The minister is to form a committee to look into the matter

--- Copenhagen airport could become a centre for cut-price flights. British discount airline Virgin Express has already started discount flights from Copenhagen, another discount airline Debonair is to follow and Copenhagen airport management says that is negotiating with another three to four discount airlines on flights from Copenhagen.
